The chorus repeats, so learn it first. Then the verses will connect around it.
That helps a lot. I'll start with the chorus.
Good. Record yourself singing, and listen for places where you hesitate. Those are the lines to practise next.
I will. It's such a fun song.
Then enjoy it. Learning a song you love never feels like work.
My parents say I spend too much time on my phone. I think it's not that much.
That's a common difference between parents and teenagers. How many hours do you spend on it each day?
Maybe three or four hours, mostly after school.
That's a lot for someone with school work. Your parents may worry that it takes time from sleep, hobbies and family.
But it's how I talk to my friends.
That's a fair point. You could suggest a plan: set times for studying and family, and allow time for friends. Showing them you can balance it will earn their trust.
I'm scared to ask my professor a question because I think it's silly.
Most professors enjoy questions, and no honest question is silly. Chances are that others in the class wonder the same thing.
What if he thinks I wasn't listening?
Try asking it in a way that shows you've thought about it: 'I understood this part, but I'm not clear about that part.' That shows effort.
My best friend's birthday is next Friday, and I want to find a gift she'll really like.
Think about what she talks about or uses a lot. What does she enjoy?
She loves reading and drawing.
Then a nice sketchbook and a set of pencils, or a book from an author she likes, would be great.
She already has lots of books.
Then art supplies might be better. A small set of good pencils and a sketchbook could be exciting, as she can use them.
Should I wrap it?
Yes. Add a handwritten note about something you like about her. That makes the gift feel personal.
Our lane wants to put on a small street play about keeping the area clean. I'm supposed to write the script.
That's a great way to share a message. Keep it short, around ten minutes, with simple scenes and a few characters.
What should the story be?
Maybe a person who throws litter and meets a funny 'garbage monster' who shows the effect of mess. It can be humorous but have a clear point at the end.
I'm joining a new school in the middle of the year and I don't know anyone.
That's a big change, and it's normal to feel nervous. The first days are the hardest. What are you most worried about?
Eating alone at lunch.
Try to introduce yourself to one or two classmates on the first day. A simple 'Hi, I'm new. Can I sit here?' works. Most children are kind to new students.
What if no one talks to me?
Give it a few days. People take time to warm up. Join an activity like a club or sports period, where you can meet others with the same interests.
I like drawing.
Then look for an art club or ask the art teacher. Sharing a hobby is a natural way to make friends.
That gives me something to look forward to.
Good. Bring a small sketchbook on the first day, and it might start a conversation.
My grandmother knows many old folk songs and I'd like to learn them from her.
What a precious thing to do. Songs like these are often not written down, so learning them keeps them alive.
Should I record her?
Ask her permission first. If she agrees, a phone recording is handy. You could also write the words in a notebook as she sings.
Texting or calling? Me and my friend disagree. I like texting and she likes calling. It's causing problems.
That can cause misunderstandings. What happens?
She says texting feels cold, and I say calls feel like too much.
Both feelings are valid. You could meet halfway: text during the week and have a longer call on weekends.
She would probably like that.
Then tell her it's because you care and want to stay close. Explaining your reason helps her not take it personally.
I'll suggest it tonight.
Good. Being open about it shows you value the friendship, and that matters more than the method.
We have guests coming, some vegetarian and some who eat non-vegetarian food. How do I plan the menu?
Make a menu where the main parts work for everyone, such as rice, dal, a vegetable dish and salad. Then add one or two non-vegetarian dishes as extras.
Should I cook them separately?
Yes, use separate pans and spoons for each, so the vegetarian dishes stay free of meat. Label the dishes if you set up a buffet.
What about dessert?
A vegetarian dessert like kheer or fruit salad suits everyone. Check if anyone has allergies, such as to nuts.
I'll ask them when I invite them.
Good. Asking early gives you time to adjust.
This makes me feel much calmer about it.
Plan the cooking order too, so that the dishes that can be made ahead are ready first.
Is it better to sit by the window or the aisle on a long journey?
It depends on what you want. The window gives you a view and something to lean on when sleeping.
And the aisle?
The aisle lets you stand up and stretch without disturbing others. Many people prefer it for long trips.
My office is so noisy that I can't focus.
That's tough. Is the noise from people talking or from machines?
Mostly people chatting and phone calls.
Headphones, even without music, can lower the noise a little. Or you could find a quiet corner or meeting room for tasks that need focus.
My boss doesn't like headphones.
Then maybe ask him if you can use a quiet room for an hour or two each day. Say it's to do your best work on difficult tasks.
I'm learning to skip rope and I keep tripping.
That happens at the start. Make sure the rope is the right length: standing on its middle, the handles should reach your armpits.
I jump too high, I think.
Yes, small hops just above the ground are enough. Keep your elbows near your body and turn the rope with your wrists.
I got a low mark in science today and I feel awful.
I'm sorry. That feels bad, especially when you studied. Did you expect a different result?
Yes, I thought I did well.
That is disappointing. Look at the paper to see where you lost marks. Sometimes it's a misread question rather than not knowing the topic.
What if my parents get upset?
Tell them yourself and show that you're ready to improve. Parents often respond better when they see you take it seriously.
I feel better. I'll ask my teacher about it.
Good. Asking the teacher shows you care about learning, and she can point out what to improve.
Thanks for listening.
Anytime. One test doesn't decide how you do in the long run.
I just got a 500-piece jigsaw puzzle and I'm overwhelmed by all those pieces.
Start with the edges. Find all the straight-sided pieces and build the frame first.
Then what?
Sort the rest by colour or pattern. Work on one section at a time, like the sky or a building, and join the sections later.
I want to collect fallen leaves in autumn and make a scrapbook.
A lovely idea. Pick leaves that are dry and not crumbly, and press them between pages of a heavy book for a week or two.
Then what?
Glue them onto thick paper, and label each with the tree's name, if you know it, and the date and place you found it.
What if I don't know the tree?
Take a photo of the whole tree and look it up in a plant guide or ask someone at a garden. Learning the names is half the fun.
I usually read mysteries. Do you think I should try something different, like a biography?
Trying something new can be refreshing. A biography is a true story, so it reads differently, but a good one has twists like a mystery.
Whose life should I read about?
Pick someone whose work or story already interests you, such as a scientist, a sportsperson or a social reformer. A shorter book is a good way to start.
Okay, but I'll still read my mysteries too.
Of course. Reading different types makes you a stronger reader, and you don't have to give up what you love.
My grandfather's eyes are weak now and he can't read his newspapers. I want to read to him.
That is a kind thing to do. Reading aloud together can become a daily habit that you both enjoy.
What should I read?
Start with the news items that he likes, such as local stories, then add short stories or a chapter from a book he loves.
I read too fast and he says he can't follow.
Slow down and pause at the end of each sentence. A calm voice is easier to listen to than a hurried one.
Should I explain difficult words?
Only if he asks. You can always stop and talk about a story after it ends, and that's often what grandparents enjoy most.
He will like that. He always tells me old stories.
Then you might hear a story behind every news item. Enjoy the time, and maybe take notes of his stories.
Our school library has started a reading challenge. We must read ten books by December.
That is a fun challenge. Ten books in a few months is doable if you plan it. How much do you read now?
About one book a month.
Then pick shorter books to start and read twenty minutes a day. A small daily habit adds up quickly.
What if I get bored of a book?
It's fine to swap it for another, as long as you finish enough in total. Keep a list of books you want to try in case you need a quick replacement.
Can I count comics?
Ask your librarian. Many libraries allow comics or picture books, but some count only novels, so check the rules.
I can't find my bookmark and I always forget my page.
A bookmark is easy to replace. Use a thin strip of card, a ribbon or an old postcard.
Folding the page corner is quicker.
It is, but it can damage the paper over time, especially in library books. A slip of paper works just as well and doesn't hurt the book.
Fair enough. I'll cut one from an old envelope.
That's perfect. You can decorate it with a drawing if you like.
For Holi this year, our colony would like to save water. Do you have ideas?
Yes, use dry colours instead of wet ones, and stay away from water balloons and hoses. Natural colours are gentler on the soil, too.
But the children love the water guns.
You could set aside a small area for them, with a limited supply from one bucket, and encourage them to refill only when needed. It keeps the fun and cuts waste.
Two new families moved into our building and I'd like to make them feel welcome.
A friendly gesture goes a long way. You could knock on their door, introduce yourself and offer help with directions or local shops.
Should I bring food?
A small plate of homemade sweets or snacks is a lovely gesture. Check first if they have any food restrictions.
What if they're shy?
Keep the visit short and warm, and don't push for a long chat. Say you're a neighbour if they need anything. They'll remember your kindness.
I'll go on Sunday afternoon, then.
A good time, since people are usually at home and relaxed. Let them settle in for a few days first.
A group of us wants to clean the lakeside near our town on Sunday. It's really dirty.
That's a great initiative. Plan it well, so the day goes smoothly. How many people are joining?
About fifteen.
Good number. Bring strong gloves, garbage bags and sticks for picking up litter. Wear closed shoes and keep an eye out for sharp objects.
What should we do with all the waste?
Ask your local municipality in advance to collect it, or arrange a vehicle to take it to the proper place. Separate plastic from other waste if you can.
Should we take our kids?
Older children can help in safe areas, but keep young ones away from the water's edge. Assign an adult to watch them.
We'll plan that. Thanks.
Good luck. Take before and after photos, and share them. They can inspire others to join the next time.
Our building's notice board is a mess. Papers are stuck everywhere.
A tidy board is easier to read. You could ask the committee if you can sort it out.
What would we do?
Remove old notices, create sections such as events, rules and lost items, and give each a clear label. Set a date on each notice so they are removed on time.
Good, I'll talk to the secretary.
Great. Offer to check the board once a week, and the system will last.
Our house is full of old newspapers piling up. Mom wants me to deal with them.
A good chore to tackle. Do you have a place to give or sell them?
The raddiwala comes on Saturdays.
Then tie them in bundles and keep them ready for him. If there are some interesting articles you want to keep, cut them out first.
My room gets so warm in the afternoon. How can I make it cooler?
Close the curtains or blinds on the sunny side to keep the heat out. Open windows in the evening when the air outside cools down.
I only have a ceiling fan.
It still helps. Make sure it runs in the right direction, and place a bowl of cold water or damp cloth near it, which can make the air feel cooler.
Is it okay to sleep with a wet cloth on the window?
Hanging a damp cloth on the window can cool the incoming air a little, as the water evaporates. Keep it away from electric points.
We'll try that. Thanks.
Also wear light cotton clothes, and keep a water bottle nearby.
A little plant corner in the living room is my plan. Where do I begin?
Choose a spot near a window with soft light. Then pick a few easy plants like money plant, snake plant or pothos.
Is there anything I should avoid?
Avoid placing plants in direct hot sun behind glass, and don't leave water sitting in saucers, since it can rot the roots.
What about the pots?
Any pot with a hole at the bottom works. If it's a decorative pot without holes, keep the plant in a plastic pot inside it.
I have a few old cups too.
Those make charming little planters, as long as you make a drainage hole in the bottom. Ask an adult to help if the cup is hard.
Good idea. I'll start this weekend.
Take it slowly with watering. Check the soil with your finger before adding more.
My little sister wants a night light in her room. Which kind is best?
A soft, warm-coloured light that she can switch off easily is ideal. It gives comfort without keeping her awake.
Should it be bright?
No, dim is enough. Too much light can make it harder to sleep.
What if she wants a character one?
That's fine as long as it's from a safe, well-made product with covered parts. Let her choose, because she'll feel more secure with something she loves.
Tomorrow is my dog's first bath at home. How do I do it?
Use lukewarm water and a gentle dog shampoo. Brush his coat first to remove tangles.
He hates water.
Then go slowly. Let him stand in the bath area with a treat, talk calmly and wet him a little at a time. Avoid his ears and eyes.
A neighbour's cat visits our house every day and sits on our porch.
That's sweet. Cats like quiet, safe places. Does she look healthy?
Yes, she's fluffy and has a collar.
Then she likely has a home. You can enjoy her visits, but let her owner know she comes here in case they worry.
Can I give her milk?
Water is the safest option. Many cats can't digest milk well, and her owner might have a feeding plan for her.
Okay, I'll put out a bowl of water.
That's kind. Also ask the owner what she may eat, so you don't upset her tummy.
I'll write to them with a note.
Good idea. A friendly note builds trust and keeps the cat safe.
I want to feed the birds on our terrace every morning. Is it a good idea?
Yes, it's lovely to watch them. Put out clean water and a small amount of grains, like millet or rice, in a shallow dish.
Won't it attract pigeons and make a mess?
Maybe, if there's a lot of food. Offer only small amounts and clean the area regularly. Water is the most valuable thing, especially in summer.
What if the cat from next door comes?
Place the dishes in an open, high spot where cats can't surprise the birds, such as on a stand or a railing with clear view.
I'll try the stand then.
Good. Place it where birds can see around, and they'll feel safe to come.
Will they really come every day?
After a week or so, they will learn the time. Keep it regular and be patient.
My friend's going away for the weekend and asked me to look after her rabbit.
That's a big responsibility, but doable. Ask her for clear instructions on food, water and cage cleaning.
What if the rabbit gets out?
Keep the door of the cage secured and any room closed. Rabbits are quick, so have a calm plan, like blocking exits and moving slowly.
Should I let him out to play?
Only if your friend says it's fine and in a safe room. Remove wires and small objects, and supervise all the time.
I'm going to the market and want to bargain, but I feel shy.
It's common to ask for a better price at markets. Do it politely and with a smile. If the seller says no, just say thanks and move on.
What if they get angry?
Most won't. Keep your tone friendly and don't argue. A fair price for both is the goal.
I'm picking a diary for the new year. There are so many designs.
Think about how you will use it. Daily notes need more pages and a firm cover, while a small notebook is easier to carry.
I'll write a little every night.
Then pick one with a page for each day or lined pages. A ribbon marker and a sturdy spine also help.
This one has a lock.
A lock is fun for privacy, but a cover that closes is also fine. Check that the paper is thick enough for pens, so ink doesn't show through.
I'll pick the lock one. It's more fun.
Good. Remember to keep the key in a safe place, so you don't get locked out of your own diary!
My son is growing fast and his uniform is already tight. Should I buy a bigger size?
A slightly bigger size can last longer, but not too big, because loose clothes can look untidy and get in the way.
The school only gives us one shop for it.
Then check if the shop allows exchanges if the size is wrong. Ask about stitching allowances, too, so that hems can be let down as he grows.
Should I buy two sets?
Two sets are practical, so one can be washed while he wears the other. Mark each piece with his name.
Good. I'll take him to try them on.
That's the best way to get a good fit. Let him move around in them to make sure they are comfortable.
Thanks, I'll do that.
Check the seams and buttons before leaving the shop, so you can exchange them immediately if needed.
I want to buy a present for my grandparents' anniversary. They have everything.
People who have everything often appreciate something personal. Is there a memory you share with them?
I love making them laugh by dancing.
Then a handwritten card with a promise of a special dance, plus a small framed photo of all of you, would delight them.
A dance would be fun. They'd record it for sure.
It can become their favourite memory. Ask them about their favourite old song and dance to it.
A friend is fasting during Navratri and I'd like to cook her something she can eat. What would be good?
That's thoughtful. Ask her which foods her family follows, because customs differ. Many people eat sabudana khichdi, kuttu rotis or potato dishes with rock salt.
Does she mind if I cook for her?
Most people appreciate it when a friend cares. Ask her gently and let her guide you with ingredients and utensils.
I'll ask tomorrow.
Good. Make sure to use clean utensils, as she may follow specific rules for her fast.
Diwali cleaning has started and my mom wants me to clean my whole room. I have so much stuff.
It's a big job, but it can feel good when you finish. Start with one corner or one shelf at a time.
Where do I put everything?
Make piles: things to keep, things to give away and things to throw out. Leave the keep pile for last, and put it back neatly.
I found old toys and books.
Those are great to donate. Many schools or community centres take books and toys that are still in good shape.
Good idea. My cousins might like them too.
Then you can give them directly. Check with their parents first, so that they have space.
I'll do that. It feels better now.
Good. Light a small diya in your clean room, and it will feel extra festive.
Our building is going carolling for Christmas. I'm not a good singer.
Carolling is about joy and togetherness, not perfect voices. In a group, you won't stand out.
But I might sing off-key.
Stand near someone who sings well and follow them. A small mistake disappears in the group sound, and people only remember the warm feeling.
I want to make Eid cards for my friends. Any ideas?
A simple card with a crescent moon and stars cut from gold paper looks pretty. Fold coloured card in half and glue the shapes on the front.
What should I write inside?
'Eid Mubarak! Wishing you joy, good food and time with family.' Then add each friend's name.
Can I make them funny?
Yes, if the friend enjoys humour. You could add a small joke about all the sweets you plan to eat.
I'll make one for my teacher too.
That'll be a lovely surprise. Keep hers simple and warm, with thanks for her help during the year.
I have a campus placement talk tomorrow and I'm so nervous.
Nerves are normal. The talk is mostly to give information. Is it a presentation or an interview?
Just a talk by a company.
Then you only need to listen and take notes. You can prepare two questions, such as what skills they look for in new joiners.
A few classmates and I want to share notes for the semester. How do we make it work?
Share a folder where each person uploads their notes for one subject, so the work is divided.
What if someone doesn't upload?
Agree on a deadline each week and remind each other kindly. If someone keeps missing it, talk privately, or divide subjects differently.
What about quality? Some people write messy notes.
Suggest a simple format: date, topic, key points and examples. Check the notes once a week and fix anything unclear.
Great, I'll propose it tomorrow.
Good idea. Start small with two subjects, and add more if it works.
I'm in a study group with five people, and the sessions turn into gossip. How do I fix it?
That's a common problem. Suggest a clear plan before each session, like 'We'll cover chapter four first.' Set a timer.
Won't that sound bossy?
Not if you phrase it as a suggestion, like 'Shall we cover this first and then take a break?' Most people agree that they should get work done.
What if they ignore me?
You can meet with just the one or two classmates who like to focus, and join the big group for fun. It's fine to want to study well.
I'll try the timer idea first.
Good. Keep the breaks short, so the gossip doesn't take over.
Let's hope it works!
Give it two or three sessions. If it works, others will follow.
Typing quickly is my goal. I only use two fingers.
That's very common. Learning to touch type, using all ten fingers, can double your speed. It takes a little practice.
Do I have to look at the keys?
At first you will, but try to use your fingers' memory by keeping them on the home row, which is the middle row of letters. Look at the screen, not the keyboard.
How long will it take?
With fifteen minutes of practice a day, many people notice improvement in two to three weeks. Start slowly and focus on accuracy first.
Are there free lessons online?
Yes, many websites offer free typing lessons and games. Choose one that gives a short daily lesson.
I'll try one tonight.
Good. Sit upright and keep your wrists relaxed, so your hands don't get tired.
I need to email my professor about missing a class. How do I start?
Keep it short and polite. Start with a greeting, state your name and class, explain briefly why you missed it and ask how to catch up.
Could you show me an example?
For example: 'Dear Professor Rao, I'm Meera from your Tuesday class. I missed today's lecture because I was unwell. Could you tell me how I can catch up on the material? Thank you, Meera.'
Should I attach a note?
Only if your college asks for one. You can mention that you can bring it, if needed.
Okay, I'll write it now.
Good. Check the subject line, and read the email once before you send it.
Thanks. It feels easier now.
It does get easier after the first one. Clear and polite is all it takes.
A stranger messaged me in a game chat and wants to be friends.
Be careful with people you only know online. It's fine to chat about the game, but don't share personal details like your school, address or photos.
He seems nice.
People can seem nice and still not be who they say. Keep talking only in the game, and tell a parent or older sibling.
What if he asks for my number?
Say no. A real friend will respect that. If he keeps asking, block him and tell a trusted adult.
I'm trying to set up a daily practice routine for singing. Where do I start?
Pick a fixed time, like the morning or just after school. Begin with five minutes of gentle humming, then sing a scale, then a song.
How long should it be?
Fifteen to twenty minutes a day is enough for beginners. Regular practice is better than one long session.
I have to sing on stage next week and I'm terrified.
It's normal to be afraid. Which song are you singing?
A popular film song.
Choose the part you know best, and practise the whole song until you can sing it without looking at the words.
What if I forget the lyrics?
Keep humming or repeat the line you remember, and join in at the next line. The audience may not notice, because they listen to the tune.
I'm thinking of joining the college choir. I've never sung in a group.
Choirs are welcoming to beginners, and singing together is a joy. They usually have a short try-out to find your voice range.
What if I'm not good enough?
Choirs value people who can listen and blend in as much as strong voices. Try the audition. If you are not selected, you can ask for feedback.
What do I need to prepare?
A short song you know well. Choose something that suits your voice, so it's comfortable to sing.
Will it be a big commitment?
Usually it means one or two rehearsals a week, so check the timetable first. Make sure it fits with your classes.
Okay. I'll go to find out.
Good. Ask them questions about the rehearsal schedule, upcoming concerts and how new members join.
It's so humid today that everything feels sticky and I can't focus.
That's tough. Humid air makes sweat evaporate slowly, so you feel hotter and stickier. Fans and cool water help.
I'm trying to study but can't sit still.
Take your books to the coolest room in the house, wear light cotton clothes and take a short break every half hour to rinse your face.
Sports day is tomorrow and the forecast says rain. We've been practising for weeks.
That's disappointing. Schools often have a backup plan, like moving events to another day or indoors. Has your teacher said anything?
Not yet.
Then wait for the announcement tomorrow morning. Meanwhile, keep your sports kit ready and check with your teacher.
What if it gets postponed?
Then you have more time to practise, and the event will still be there. Your work isn't wasted.
Okay, that makes me feel a bit better.
Good. Keep your kit ready, and use the extra days to rest your legs and fix anything you want to polish.
I like walking in the morning, but winter mornings are so foggy.
Fog makes it hard to see and be seen, so choose a safe route. Walk on footpaths, or in a park if one is nearby.
I wear dark clothes usually.
Switch to brighter colours or add a reflective strip. It helps drivers see you from a distance.
Should I wait until the fog clears?
That's a good option. Mid-morning is usually clearer. If you walk early, take a friend and stay on familiar paths.
My manager asked me to present our project to the whole department. I've never spoken to so many people.
That's a good sign that he trusts you. Prepare a short outline with three main points, and practise aloud.
What if people ask difficult questions?
It's fine to say, 'That's a good question. I'll check and get back to you.' Honesty is better than guessing.
A coworker I really liked is leaving the company. Everyone wants to do something for her.
A farewell is a kind gesture. What does she like?
She loves chocolate and travelling.
Then you could give a small box of chocolates and a card from the whole team. A travel journal would be a nice, personal gift too.
We could also have a team lunch.
Yes, a team lunch lets everyone say goodbye together. Pick a day and place that suits most people and invite her.
Should I make a speech?
A short one is enough. Mention one thing she did well and thank her for her support. Keep it warm and simple.
I'm a bit emotional already.
That's natural. Being sincere matters more than being perfect, and she will probably be touched.
I planted some bean seeds last week and they've started sprouting!
That is great news. Seeing the first green shoot is exciting. Where did you plant them?
In a pot on the window.
A sunny window is perfect for beans. Water them lightly when the top soil is dry, and give them a stick or string to climb as they grow.
How fast will they grow?
Beans grow quickly, often a few centimetres a week. In a month or two you may see flowers and later pods.
There were so many butterflies in our garden today. Why are they here now?
Butterflies come out when the weather is warm and flowers are in bloom, because flowers give them nectar to drink.
They seem to like the yellow flowers.
Many butterflies are attracted to bright colours, and yellow and orange are popular. If you plant more flowers like these, more butterflies will visit.
There's a surprise coming for my birthday tomorrow, I can tell, and I'm too excited to sleep.
What fun. Is it okay to guess what it might be?
I think it's a trip to the zoo.
That would be a great one. Try not to ask your family too many questions. Let them enjoy planning it.
It's so hard to wait.
Do something calm tonight, like reading or a small drawing. A warm drink and an early bedtime will make tomorrow come faster.
Okay, I'll try that.
Enjoy the surprise tomorrow, whatever it is.
I'm feeling grateful today, and I'm not sure why. Everything is just fine.
That's a nice feeling, and ordinary good days deserve to be noticed. It's good that you paused to feel it.
I want to do something with this feeling.
You could write a thank-you note to someone who helped you, or note three good things from today in your diary. It makes the feeling last.
I'll thank my mother. She's done a lot for me.
She'll be happy to hear it. Tell her one specific thing she did, so that it feels real.
I think I'll cook dinner tomorrow too.
That's a thoughtful gift. Plan something simple that you can cook well, and let her relax.
I'm smiling just thinking about it.
Hold on to that. Gratitude is something to practise, and it grows when you do.
I tried pottery at a workshop today and my pot collapsed. It was so funny.
That's a very common first experience. Clay needs even pressure and a steady hand. Did you enjoy it?
Yes! I want to try again.
Then do. The second pot will likely be better, because your hands now know how the clay feels. Keep the walls even and don't make them too thin.
I've started playing chess online but I lose every game.
That's normal at the start. Beginners learn a lot from losses. Do you know the basics, such as how pieces move?
Yes, but I forget to protect my pieces.
That's a very common mistake. Before each move, ask yourself, 'What is my opponent threatening?' It takes a few seconds and saves many pieces.
Is there a way to practise?
Yes, you can try short puzzles, which show a position and ask for the best move. They train you to spot ideas quickly.
I'll start with puzzles.
Good. After each game, look at where you made your first big mistake, and try to learn from it.
I have my first group presentation in class tomorrow and I don't know if I should make slides.
Slides can help, but they aren't compulsory. What is the topic?
The water cycle. We're a team of four.
Then a few simple slides with pictures of rain, clouds and rivers would help. Keep the text short and each person explains one stage.
Okay, I'll make four slides.
Good, one per person. Practise passing the talk smoothly from one speaker to the next.
My mother wants to learn to use video calls to talk to her sister abroad.
That's lovely. Show her how to open the app, tap on her sister's name and press the video button.
She gets nervous about pressing the wrong thing.
Reassure her that she can't break the phone by tapping. Practise with you in the next room, calling her, so she can learn the steps.
I'd like to learn how to make a basic omelette without breaking it.
A simple omelette is easy once you know the steps. Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, heat a little oil in a pan on medium heat and pour them in.
Mine always turns into scrambled eggs.
That happens when you stir it. Let the egg set for a minute, then gently fold it in half with a spatula and cook the other side briefly.
What about the heat?
Medium or low is best. Too high and it browns before it cooks inside, and it will break when you flip it.
My friend borrowed my notes and then said she didn't need them. I feel used.
That can feel odd, especially if you took the time to share. Do you think she meant to upset you?
I don't think so, but it hurt.
Then let her know, in a friendly way: 'I was happy to share my notes, but I felt a bit hurt when you said you didn't need them.' Many people don't realise how they sound.
Long-distance running is hard for me because I get a stitch after a short while.
Many beginners feel that. A slower pace usually helps. Are you breathing evenly?
Probably not. I breathe fast.
Try slowing your pace so you can speak in short sentences, and breathe in steadily through the nose and mouth.
Should I walk in between?
Yes, mixing short runs with walking is a good way to build up. Run for two minutes, walk for one, and repeat.
I'll try that on Sunday.
Good. Don't eat a heavy meal just before running, and drink water before and after.
We're going to visit my uncle in a village for a week, and my city friends say I'll be bored.
Village visits can be wonderful. There is often a slower pace, lots of fresh air and plenty to see.
I don't know what to do all day.
Walk through the fields, help with small farm jobs, watch how the food is grown and cooked, and ask your uncle about his life. You may enjoy it more than you expect.
I can take my sketchbook.
Good idea. Sketch the animals, plants and houses. At the end of the week, you'll have a lovely record of the trip.
